audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 is marked 'Skill' while its own why says 'Level 6 his R root and gank setup swing the phase to him', and the packet chart gives that stage to Maokai.
audit.why: The row argues Maokai wins and the token says neither does. The window summaries then omit Level 6 from his side entirely, so the player is told to fight in a stage the same page says he loses.
audit.corrected: Flipped win[4] and phases[4].side/rating together, and rewrote breakdown.spikes and report[2].t to list Level 6 as his.

audit.why: Twisted Advance is 14/13/12/11/10 — 14s at rank 1, and 11s is what it costs at rank 4. In a lane whose whole plan is 'fight when the root is down', a three-second error is the difference between a free all-in and eating the root.
audit.corrected: Rewrote report[5].t with 14s and the untargetable window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six fields put Maokai's abilities in the wrong slots: 'his W Sapling and E Nature's Grasp root setup', 'his E root and Sapling', 'Land E Nature's Grasp or R root', 'roots you repeatedly with E and R'. Nothing mentions that Twisted Advance makes him untargetable.
audit.why: Twisted Advance (W) is the root — a targeted dash that makes him untargetable in transit. Sapling Toss (E) is zone control with a knockup and slow, no root. Nature's Grasp (R) is the advancing wall. The untargetable frames matter most: Demacian Justice spent into his W dash is simply lost, and a player told to 'silence his E root' will hold the silence for a spell that does not exist. His R also creates terrain across your retreat and Garen has no dash, so Flash is for the wall, not for damage.
audit.corrected: Rewrote spikes[0].text, spikes[3].text, content.early, content.late, wants.you[0], wants.foe[0], dontsFull[2].d and report[5].t.

audit.why: Executioner's Calling first back and Mortal Reminder third is right — Sap Magic heals him on every empowered attack and the cooldown shortens each time he casts or is hit by a spell, which is exactly the sustain Grievous Wounds cuts.

edits.after: Late the matchup is his: stacked HP and armour absorb your whole Judgment rotation, Twisted Advance and Nature's Grasp strip your engage, and he peels his carries away, so shift to sidelane pressure rather than trying to kill him.

notes: Bramble Smash (Q) knocks back and slows on a 7s cooldown at rank 1 — Decisive Strike breaks the slow outright. No in-band field existed to carry that; it is the best unstated advantage Garen has in this lane. tldr/focus.text/winCon carry OCR debris ('Garen Top Lane Matchup Database (1-70) 60') and both name Sapling/Bramble Smash as the focus when Twisted Advance is what actually decides the lane.
